item.title: Re: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
Hey author, just pitching in my 2 cents.

This is really out of character for Anderson Robotics. Though this is not the first time they make an exoskeleton, it's certainly the first time they would be making a weapon of war! They're mostly known for making consumer grade products and fancy gizmos for the wealthy. A fighting exoskeleton that commits war crimes is definitely not something they would do. But that isn't to say Anderson Robotics isn't a moral bastion. Vincent Anderson, the founder, is known for being a cheat and a bit of a ruffian. There's also the fact that most AR products are powered by souls, which can lead to ethical questions.

Then there's the issue of the idea. Like zyn said, it's very typical of exoskeleton tropes and doesn't have much of interest going on for it.

item.title: Re: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look.

I'll be honest, I personally don't see this working. Not only is the typical "super suit that messes with the person wearing it" trope extremely commonly seen in popular media and the SCP wiki in general, the portrayal of the Foundation here is questionable to the point of breaking suspension of disbelief for me.

+ show block
– hide block

As a general note, I'm not overly familiar with Anderson Robotics, so I can't comment much about the inclusion of that GoI as the backstory here. For me as a reader the mention of that GoI doesn't contribute meaningfully to the narrative.

My main issue with the premise is pretty much the entirety of this:

Before the foundation could class him as Thaumiel, they tested the suit's abilities and the soldier's control over the suit. After the suit was tested it was found valuable in containing SCP's and helping in raids. He was classed a Thaumiel SCP and assigned to MTF Alpha-9 ("Last Hope") To be trained further and then used in the field. He was shipped to Site-06-3 awaiting deployment.

Having something be useful for containing anomalies is not the same as said something actively containing anomalies. Anomalous gear that could help MTFs fight, for example, would not be considered Thaumiel. The fact that the suit is conveniently "valuable" for containing anomalies despite the person having no Foundation experience whatsoever makes the character/suit seem like a Mary Sue setup. Fast-tracking the guy immediately to Thaumiel and assigning him to Last Hope for training (ideally he should be trained before being put on that MTF, given he's starting from near zero familiarity with Foundation team mechanics) diverts the attention from "feel bad for this guy, he's traumatized by the suit" to "he's just yet another overpowered character solely existing to be shoehorned onto Alpha-9" territory.

The suit's abilities are explained with addendums and mission logs.

I myself am not really interested in a laundry list of the suit's abilities. We already have lots of anomalous/super high-tech suits in the Foundation'verse, including the suit Agent Adams tests in this Resurrection tale: http://www.scpwiki.com/number-one-with-a-bullet

My idea is unique because of two reasons. 1, the SCP's abilities. It's super-human strength, resistance to small bullets and kinetic energy. I have yet to see a robotic SCP with such abilities on the site.

Having the exact specific abilities not be exactly addressed by another suit doesn't really make this unique. It's still fundamentally a suit with a bunch of kind of typical abilities. The reason Adams's suit portrayal works in the aforementioned tale is because the focus isn't on the suit's abilities, but rather Adams's reactions and training and struggles to learn how to cope with wearing the suit in different dangerous scenarios. If the only mechanical difference yours presents is "mine is robotic and has different minutiae qualities", that's not going to be enough to impress the audience.

And 2, It's friendly-ness towards humans and it's will to help them with raids, containment and more that they ask for.

One of the main reasons we don't have much of this sort of thing on the mainsite isn't because no one's ever written them, but rather people have written them but the audience hasn't liked the portrayal. Super powerful convenient friendly suits are kind of lazy writing and reminiscent of childish overpowered characters that aren't taken seriously because of how convenient and easy it is for them to be put in a heroic spotlight where they seemingly can do/experience no wrong.

Part of that is reflected here: the Foundation immediately tests, recruits, and promotes the guy without any sort of suspicion or counseling. The point of the story then seems to be just to set up yet another super cool for no reason character, rather than telling a compelling story that will convince readers to care about the individual on a relatable level. cybersqyd already mentioned this in the post above and it doesn't look like it was properly addressed.

Remember, just because you as the author really really want the Foundation to think your character is cool does not mean it automatically makes sense for in-universe personnel to immediately trust the guy.

Personally I would recommend that you shelve this concept and return to it after you've gotten one or two successful mainsite works submitted. Not only would this require a lot of editing to be workable, it's also concept material that an experienced author would have some difficulty with given both the large number of similar attempts that have gone through the site and the community tendency to regard super suits with skepticism and not intrigue.

If you really want to work with this, I would say definitely remove the Thaumiel rating, remove the Alpha-9 membership, and focus on the Anderson Robotics backstory and the person in the suit as a person and not yet another random asset the Foundation will throw at anomalies without question.

item.title: Re: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

The first suit was tested, the U.S. army closed the deal off after they saw what horrible things the suit can do.

What horrible things? There's kinda an implication that this can do many different things but I don't really have a feel for what.

Only 3 were made two are still lost and the third one a soldier still wears.

What does 'lost' mean here? Like, 'missing'? Or 'destroyed'? If it's the first, why is no-one else looking for it?

This feels…a little unsatisfying to me. On one level, there's some thematic weirdness: there's this like, sense that the SCP is a dude who just, wants to do his best and is a big dang hero that everyone loves, except the US army found it too horrifying to use and so there's this disconnect between the angle of 'the foundation will do anything and resort to any means' which feels kinda horrifying and the angle of this dude just being super nice and cool and chill, which feels kinda heartwarming.

On another level: you don't really do anything interesting with this; there's a long investigation section at the start that feels kinda uninteresting because none of the discoveries are particularly novel (since, the discovery would be after the description here: we already know the foundation found a suit and there's a person in it cos guess what, we already read the description) and then there's a vague thing about him joining an MTF. This isn't a bad thing to happen but it's under-utilised: there's no like, extensive training sequence and determined work by the SCP towards convincing the Foundation he can be helpful and uncertainty of whether he'd achieve that; but there's also no real like…cool things happening as a result of them being in a MTF; there's no 'mission log' or anything and I'm left feeling like this just…doesn't have the narrative meat to it for it to work.

Circling back to the themes: I'm really not a fan of the kinda, glorification of the military throughout this. This is, obviously, a personal thing but it's very possible that I just wouldn't like something this 'boo yah go soldiers' even if you had executed it well.

item.title: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action.

Elevator Pitch: The elite operative is a soldier that is trapped inside a suit. The suit has many abilities some are cruel then others. But the soldier got stuck after testing the suit. No matter what he or others do he cannot be opened. he is stuck in a metallic cell that can walk

Central Narrative: The story starts in a Anderson robotics factory. Anderson robotics made a deal with the U.S. army to create suits that would give soldiers anomalous abilities. The first suit was tested, the U.S. army closed the deal off after they saw what horrible things the suit can do.It broke many geneva convention rules and the U.S. army did not want such suits. Only 3 were made two are still missing and the third one a soldier still wears. The foundation is still looking for the two missing suits. The SCP foundation heard about the suits and found a suit with the soldier inside. Verbal communication was not affective since any sound that the soldier would make is drowned by the heavy metal suit. All attempts to get the soldier out of the suit are in-affective. After finding out the soldier could not be freed, he was interviewed via radio.

+ Show text
- Hide text

The foundation knew nothing about the suit. And since it was made by Anderson robotics they can't trust the suit either it was sent to humanoid containment in site 06-3, tests about his abilities and his suit will begin in site 06-3 they will be explained with addendums and some test logs. And since Anderson robotics built the suit they will check if the suit is sentient or manipulative. And still they try to free the soldier so he could have is normal life again. To keep the soldier sane and or happier therapists were called to talk to him, and he sent letters to his family stating he is in iraq to keep the suit a secret.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The attention grabber here is the miss-trust from the foundation towards the soldier. Even though the suit is causing this suspicion, everyone is suspicious of his suit. Since Anderson robotics create questionable robots. They suspect his suit to be controlling him and are doing everything in their power to help him get out.

Additional Notes: None
